findings.issue_text: I18n.fallbacks now enabled in all environments including test, so missing translations silently fall back instead of raising I18n::MissingTranslation, masking real translation gaps in CI (config/initializers/i18n.rb:9-12)

ensure_loaded! only runs in the controller request path; mailers, background jobs, and other entry points can attempt fallback lookups against unloaded locales, producing spurious I18n::MissingTranslation errors (app/controllers/application_controller.rb:158, config/initializers/i18n.rb:19-21)

Check-then-load race in ensure_loaded!/translate under threaded servers: @loaded_locales.include? followed by load_locale is not atomic, so concurrent threads can observe a partially populated translation store (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:63-65)

FallbackLocaleList discards the default locale hierarchy fallback, so regional variants like de-DE no longer fall back to their parent language de, causing users to see English text where parent-language translations exist (config/initializers/i18n.rb:15-17)

Synchronous translation loading via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! in set_locale adds per-request cold-load latency (DB + file loading) in the hot path instead of at boot, with @loaded_locales growing per-process
FallbackLocaleList#[] constructs a fresh fallback array and reads SiteSetting.default_locale on every translation miss with no memoization, causing up to 3x backend lookups on missing keys
ensure_loaded! has a thread-unsafe check-then-act on @loaded_locales, allowing concurrent load_locale execution and duplicated work/races when invoked from the request path

FallbackLocaleList is an empty Hash subclass returning computed values from [] only, breaking the Hash contract — iteration/inspection sees nothing and hash mutations are silent no-ops, a correctness hazard with perf side effects

goldens.comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

adjudication_records.issue_text: I18n.fallbacks now enabled in all environments including test, so missing translations silently fall back instead of raising I18n::MissingTranslation, masking real translation gaps in CI (config/initializers/i18n.rb:9-12)

adjudication.rationale: The new global initializer `config/initializers/i18n.rb` unconditionally includes `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` and sets `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`, which will apply in all Rails environments (including test) since initializers run everywhere. That means lookups can fall back to `SiteSetting.default_locale` and then `:en` (`FallbackLocaleList#[]`), potentially hiding missing translations in the primary locale during CI. The diff doesn’t show any environment-specific gating to keep tests strict.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ensure_loaded! only runs in the controller request path; mailers, background jobs, and other entry points can attempt fallback lookups against unloaded locales, producing spurious I18n::MissingTranslation errors (app/controllers/application_controller.rb:158, config/initializers/i18n.rb:19-21)

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes locale fallback loading explicit via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` (ApplicationController#set_locale) and defines `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` to call `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for the fallback chain (config/initializers/i18n.rb:19-21). However, that ensure step is only invoked from the controller request path; nothing in the diff shows mailers/background jobs/other entry points calling `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`. Given the TranslateAccelerator only guarantees loading for the active locale unless explicitly ensured (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb), fallback lookups from non-controller contexts can hit unloaded fallback locales and miss translations that exist but were never loaded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Check-then-load race in ensure_loaded!/translate under threaded servers: @loaded_locales.include? followed by load_locale is not atomic, so concurrent threads can observe a partially populated translation store (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:63-65)
matched_golden_ids: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same thread-safety problem: @loaded_locales is used for lazy loading without synchronization, and the include?/load_locale sequence is a non-atomic check-then-act that can race under concurrent threads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FallbackLocaleList discards the default locale hierarchy fallback, so regional variants like de-DE no longer fall back to their parent language de, causing users to see English text where parent-language translations exist (config/initializers/i18n.rb:15-17)

adjudication.rationale: In config/initializers/i18n.rb, FallbackLocaleList#[] hard-codes the fallback chain to `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` (lines ~15-17), which omits the parent-language fallback that Rails/I18n’s default fallbacks (previously enabled via `config.i18n.fallbacks = true`) typically provide for regional variants (e.g., `:"de-DE"` -> `:de`). With this change, if `de-DE` is missing a key but `de` has it, the chain will skip `de` and may fall through to the site default / English instead, matching the reported regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Synchronous translation loading via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! in set_locale adds per-request cold-load latency (DB + file loading) in the hot path instead of at boot, with @loaded_locales growing per-process

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` directly in `ApplicationController#set_locale`, putting locale loading on the request path (app/controllers/application_controller.rb). The new `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for `[I18n.locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]` (config/initializers/i18n.rb), and `TranslateAccelerator#ensure_loaded!` keeps `@loaded_locales` as an ever-growing per-process array with no eviction (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb). This is a diff-grounded performance/behavior concern (potential cold-load latency and unbounded locale cache growth), not a correctness bug proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FallbackLocaleList#[] constructs a fresh fallback array and reads SiteSetting.default_locale on every translation miss with no memoization, causing up to 3x backend lookups on missing keys

adjudication.rationale: In config/initializers/i18n.rb, FallbackLocaleList#[] builds a new array each call and fetches SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym each time: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`. There is no memoization/caching of the fallback chain per locale or per default_locale value, so repeated fallback resolution will redo this work. Also, the fallback chain explicitly contains up to 3 locales, so missing translations will trigger multiple fallback attempts by design (though the exact number of backend lookups depends on I18n internals beyond the diff). This is a performance/architecture concern rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ensure_loaded! has a thread-unsafe check-then-act on @loaded_locales, allowing concurrent load_locale execution and duplicated work/races when invoked from the request path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ensure_loaded!(locale)` in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` that does `@loaded_locales ||= []` and then `load_locale locale unless @loaded_locales.include?(locale)`. This is a classic check-then-act pattern with no synchronization, and the new call site in `ApplicationController#set_locale` (`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`) makes it more likely to be hit from concurrent requests. The diff alone doesn’t prove a user-visible failure (it may only cause duplicated locale loads), but it is a concrete, diff-grounded concurrency/performance concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FallbackLocaleList is an empty Hash subclass returning computed values from [] only, breaking the Hash contract — iteration/inspection sees nothing and hash mutations are silent no-ops, a correctness hazard with perf side effects

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` and overrides `def [](locale)` to always return a computed array (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`) without consulting/storing any underlying Hash state. That means the object will behave like an “empty” hash for iteration/inspection while `[]` returns dynamic values, and any future attempts to mutate/cache via normal Hash semantics (e.g., `fallbacks[loc]=...`) would not affect reads. This is a real design/correctness hazard grounded in the diff, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it breaks runtime behavior since I18n may only rely on `fallbacks[locale]`.
